businessModel: Bundled free with Fire tablets, Fire TV and Echo Show; supports Amazon’s device and content ecosystem
updateCadence: Several builds a month across parallel Chromium branches
summary: Silk is the default browser on Amazon’s Fire devices. It began in 2011 with a cloud-accelerated split-browser design and is now a Chromium-based browser with Alexa control, private tabs and Amazon account backup.
bestFor: Fire tablet and Fire TV owners
notFor: People who need extensions, ad blocking or a password manager
Anyone who wants strong privacy defaults

pros.title: Built into Fire devices
pros.detail: Preinstalled on Fire tablets, Fire TV and Echo Show.

pros.title: Current Chromium base
pros.detail: Version 152 uses Chromium 152, so modern sites work.

pros.title: Alexa voice control
pros.detail: Alexa and the Fire TV remote can control video and music.

pros.title: Private tabs and local history
pros.detail: History is stored on the device and can be cleared.

cons.title: No extensions or ad blocker
cons.detail: Amazon’s docs say Silk has no add-on support and no built-in ad blocking.

cons.title: Amazon account tie-in
cons.detail: Optional customised recommendations send browsing history to Amazon.

cons.title: Closed and device-bound
cons.detail: Proprietary, and mainly useful on Amazon hardware.

faq.q: Does Silk still use Amazon’s cloud to speed up pages?
faq.a: The original 2011 split-browser design did, with an option to turn it off; current docs describe a Chromium-based browser.

faq.q: Can I install ad blockers in Silk?
faq.a: No. Amazon says Silk does not support extensions or add-ons.
Fire tablets can back up settings and bookmarks to the Amazon cloud; full sync is not documented officially.

timeline.event: Launched on the original Kindle Fire with cloud-split design

switching.note: A Chrome extension can save Chrome bookmarks to an Amazon account for Silk.

spec.patchLag: About 6 weeks behind Chrome by version number

battery: Tablets are efficient for casual use
resourceControls: No tab or memory controls documented
patchSpeed: Chromium 152 in Oct 2026, a few weeks behind
media: Video on Fire TV and tablets

featureNotes.telemetryOptOut: Recommendations setting can be turned off
featureNotes.syncBookmarks: Backup and Restore to Amazon cloud
featureNotes.importData: Bookmark import via a Chrome extension
